messages:
Maya: Quick obs check before I take on-call — where's the fastest way to grab a representative TTFT vs tokens/sec sample for the /v1/generate route? I need p50/p95/p99 numbers + one slow trace to attach to a bug report. Any dashboards or panels to bookmark?

Samir: Start with the 'Request latency by route' grafana panel (top-left of the 'Inference/Latency' dashboard). Filter by route=/v1/generate and model=redwood-v2-small. Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/inf-latency/inference-latency?orgId=1

Samir: Quick PromQL to get p50/p95/p99 TTFT (tokens path):
```
histogram_quantile(0.50, sum(rate(ttft_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ttft_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(ttft_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Replace route/model labels as needed. For tokens/sec use `sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total{route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (instance)` and divide by concurrent requests if you want per-request.

Samir: For a slow trace sample, click a high-latency row in the table panel → 'open trace in jaeger'. Jaeger link base: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/search. Look for traces with big `decoder::kv_cache_miss` spans.

Maya: Awesome, thanks. Any quick checklist for isolating whether it's batching vs KV cache thrash?

Samir: Checklist (short):
- Check tokens/sec spike coincident with TTFT increase (same time window)
- Inspect decoder span durations in Jaeger (is time in attention / matmul?)
- See if requests were routed to a different pool (node label change) in the same minutes
- Check recent deploys around the window (OpsBot will post deploys)

Lin: Heads up — we saw a recurring p95 blip for /v1/generate around 02:10 UTC yesterday tied to a model roll with different kv-cache config. Proposed alert tweak: move p95 threshold from 850ms -> 1.2s for blue pool for 72h while we validate rollback metrics. Filed PR: https://git.internal/redwood/alerts/pulls/194

Lin: Proposal rationale: transient rollout spikes were causing noisy pages. We'll monitor with a temporary suppression rule and then revert. Paging policy in PR explains tagging.

Alex: FWIW I rolled back the model patch last night at 02:25 — saw immediate p95 improvement. I left a note in the release channel. If you want, I can dump a couple of slow traces to the bug. :thumbsup:

Maya: Please dump 2 samples (p95 and p99) and attach to the bug. Also add which instance/node they hit. Tagging @Samir for trace interpretation. :eyes:

OpsBot: [deploy] service: inference-runtime, env: prod, version: v2026.3.14-rc3, user: alex — started 2026-03-10T02:14:22Z — https://deploys.redwood.internal/infra/12345

Samir: I'll pull two traces and attach spans of interest (decoder, attention, kernel compilation if present). Expect links in ~15m.

Maya: Thanks — ping me when done and I'll paste into the bug and notify the customer-facing team.

Alex: Done: attached two trace links in the bug — p95: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/trace/abcd1234, p99: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/trace/efgh5678. Instances: node-22, node-07.

Samir: Quick note for the runbook: when triaging TTFT spikes, always check (1) route filter, (2) model variant, (3) node labels (gpu type), (4) any concurrent large-batch jobs. Adding runbook PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/pulls/33

Maya: Perfect. Closing this mini-handoff — I'll take on-call and monitor the p95 alert after Lin's temporary tweak. If anyone sees noise, ping me. :coffee:
